name: GATE Overflow CS Test Series 2026 | Verbal Aptitude | Shallow Test 1

question.text:
If "NSTHGRB" stands for 'bright sun' and "YKSLB" stands for 'blue sky', which of the following stands for 'warm breeze'?

  1. ZBRMRW
  2. EEEAAA
  3. ZRBMRW
  4. WRMBRZ

The decision to implement the new policy came from the board of directors, ______?

  1. didn't it
  2. did it
  3. didn't they
  4. hasn't it

If "tessklo" means "bookshelf" and "klotin" means "bookstore" and "sintin" means "storefront", which of the following would mean "library"?

  1. sklosin
  2. tinsint
  3. tessin
  4. klotess

Choose the best alternative to replace the underlined part in the following sentence:

The sunlight $\underline{\text{streamed through}}$ the curtains.

  1. filtering into
  2. bouncing off
  3. melting onto
  4. shining through

The questions given below consist of a pair of related words followed by four pairs of words. Select the pair that best expresses the relation to the original pair.
Chef: Cuisine

  1. Painter: Palette
  2. Author: Book
  3. Musician: Instrument
  4. Sommelier: Wine

Choose from the options the word most similar in meaning to the given one:
Convincing

  1. persuasive
  2. uncertain
  3. ambiguous
  4. hesitant

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.
Emma has planned to _______her job in New York and relocate to California.
  1. transition
  2. resign
  3. withdraw
  4. excel

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word:
After years of collaboration, he finally decided to ____ with his business partner.

  1. dissolve ties
  2. end collaboration
  3. terminate the partnership
  4. conclude the association

From among the given sentences, pick the grammatically correct one:

  1. She has been studying for two months.
  2. She has been studying since two months.
  3. She has been studying from two months.
  4. She has been studying over two months.

From among the given sentences, pick the grammatically INCORRECT one:

  1. She suggested to visit the museum.
  2. They arrived at the station early.
  3. We enjoyed the concert thoroughly.
  4. He can speak three languages fluently.

From among the given sentences, pick the grammatically correct one:

  1. Blowing out the candles, she made a wish.
  2. The test results showed that she scored more higher than her classmates.
  3. His actions in the game were more skillful then his opponents.
  4. Running quickly, he reached the finish line ahead of the other competitors.

From among the given sentences, pick the grammatically correct one.

  1. He suggested me to try it.
  2. They were happy on hearing the news.
  3. We discussed about the plan.
  4. She avoids to eat sweets.

___________________ he not called you in advance, you would have been late.
 

  1. If
  2. Were
  3. Had
  4. Could

Which of the following cannot be logically inferred from the given passage?

Recent studies have shown that regular exercise can improve cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of chronic diseases such as diabetes and hypertension.
Eating a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins is also essential for maintaining overall health. Additionally, adequate sleep and stress management techniques play a crucial role in promoting well-being.

  1. Regular exercise can decrease the risk of chronic diseases.
  2. Consuming a balanced diet can improve cardiovascular health.
  3. Sleep has no impact on overall health.
  4. Stress management techniques are ineffective in promoting well-being.

The employee ____to the day when he could leave his current job.

  1. had envisioned
  2. envisions
  3. is envisioning
  4. will envision

When he started his business, he was hardly the ________entrepreneur he later proved to be, as he had strong support from experienced mentors.

  1. fledgling
  2. audacious
  3. amateurish
  4. hesitant

1. All lions are carnivores.
  2. Some animals are carnivores.
  3. All animals are lions.

If statements (I) and (II) are TRUE, then (III) will be:

  1. Insufficient data
  2. True
  3. Not applicable
  4. False

The teacher does not agree ______ the proposal put forward by the students.

  1. with
  2. in
  3. to
  4. by

From among the given sentences, pick the grammatically INCORRECT one:
   
  1. She is good at playing piano.
  2. He is interested in learning Spanish.
  3. I look forward to meet you.
  4. They decided to stay at home.

Fact: All birds can fly.

Which of the following is a logically valid conclusion based on the above statement?

  1. It is a bird.
  2. It cannot fly.
  3. It can fly.
  4. It is not a bird.


  1. If (I), then (III).
  2. If (III), then (I).
  3. If (II), then (IV).
  4. If (IV), then (II).

A rapidly $\underline{river}$ had carved its way through the ancient $\underline{valley}$. The underlined words are ________.
                       
  1. prepositions
  2. pronouns
  3. conjunctions
  4. nouns

Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below to complete the sentence:

Stealing from one's employer can be considered __________.

  1. perjury
  2. embezzlement
  3. homicide
  4. arson

Your decision should be based on facts and not on ________.

  1. opinions
  2. conjectures
  3. assumptions
  4. prejudices

The security personnel were directed to $\underline{restrict}$ the protesters until the situation was resolved.
The underlined word is closest in meaning to:

  1. release
  2. isolate
  3. overlook
  4. liberate

Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below to complete the sentence:

The charity organization focuses on ________ hunger in impoverished communities.

  1. addressing
  2. ignoring
  3. exacerbating
  4. advocating

Choose the most appropriate alternative from the options given below to complete the sentence:

The family chose to _________ during their vacation to save money for their future plans.

  1. indulge
  2. economize
  3. squander
  4. lavish

The questions given below consist of a pair(s) of related words followed by four pairs of words. Select the pair that best expresses the relation to the original pair.

Radiology: Medicine
 

  1. Botany: Plants
  2. Optometry: Vision
  3. Zoology: Animals
  4. Geology: Rocks

In the following sentence, phrases are marked as P, Q, and R. One of the parts may contain an error or may not be acceptable in standard written communication.
Select the part containing an error.Choose D as your answer if there is no error.

After  a long day at work, Sarah decided to unwind by watching her favorite TV show (P), reading a book, and (Q) to take a warm bath (R).

  1. P
  2. Q
  3. R
  4. No error

If you don't practice regularly, it will be difficult to ____.

  1. keep up
  2. keep in
  3. keep on
  4. keep at

Choose from the options the word most similar in meaning to the given one:
Ebullient

  1. exuberant
  2. restrained
  3. cavernous
  4. ebbed
